content.value:
The Chargers unfortunately fell short against the Jets 27-24 on Sunday and dropped to 1-9 on the year with seven games remaining. A miraculous late game run to push for a winning record is now impossible and all of you who held out hope for such a thing can now finally let that one go.

Another loss further reinforced the Chargers as one of the league’s worst. With a chance to get out of the bottom three in the league, the defense unfortunately could not find any decent footing as the Jets went the entire game without a single punt.

Offensively it was a better day for Justin Herbert and that unit, but overall it wasn’t enough to beat a previously 2-win Jets team.

With that said, let’s get into the rankings from Week 12.

NFL.com – #29

“After finally winning a game in Week 10, the Chargers returned to their former selves, minus the crushing turnovers. A remarkably quick game saw just 12 possessions combined between the two teams, and the Chargers didn’t quite value them as much as they should have in Sunday’s loss. A complete lack of urgency while facing a 10-point deficit frustrated everyone taking the time to watch this game and included a sequence of snaps that featured a flea flicker on third-and-2, a speed option run by a quarterback (Justin Herbert) who had already taken too many hits, and a pace that ate up nearly eight minutes of time in the fourth quarter. This is an unserious team that unsurprisingly didn’t regain possession after that marathon scoring drive and might not win another game if it continues operating like this.”

Pro Football Talk – #30

“Will Jim Harbaugh be back for 2027?” – Mike Florio

ESPN – #31

“The best player on the Chargers this season is playing out his rookie deal, so the best candidate for an extension is fairly obvious. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Tuipulotu leads the team with 37 pressures through Sunday. Are the Chargers willing to pay him top edge money, which could be close to $35 million per year? Only time will tell.” – Aaron Schatz

The Athletic – #31

“The sooner this season ends, the better. And this game lasted only 2 hours, 40 minutes, the shortest of the year. The Chargers and Jets had only six possessions apiece Sunday. New York scored on its first five, marking a rare occasion when the defense let down Los Angeles. The Chargers are now next to last in the league in offensive EPA per drive (minus-0.80).” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff

CBS Sports – #31

“After winning at Baltimore, they were back to being the Chargers again, losing to the Jets. This team has to make changes.”

Sports Illustrated – #31

“On the MMQB pod, Albert Breer breathlessly details the potential death knell in the Jim Harbaugh era: a long, meandering drive to nowhere with the game on the line.” – Conor Orr

Yahoo Sports – #32

“Good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again.“

“At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It’s not much, especially in a loss. But it’s not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.”

Sporting News – #32

“The Chargers played a clean game for the most part, but still lost to the Jets because of a key stat: Giving up six sacks on Justin Herbert. He’s been dropped 39 times in 10 games, the most in the league. The offensive line injuries continue to have lingering effects.” – Vinnie Iyer

content.value:
The Chargers went and won their first game against the Ravens in Week 11 but followed that with yet another loss this past Sunday against the Jets. They’re now 1-9 with seven games to go.

If the Chargers continue their losing ways, they will stay in the mix for one of the top players in the upcoming draft class. Obviously Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith is the crown jewel of the group, but will the Bolts truly have a shot at taking Smith if they don’t pick number one overall?

To be quite honest, yes, they could.

Quarterbacks always end up being the biggest priority amongst the league’s worst teams. If the Chargers end up picking at No. 3 — like they do in this new mock at The Athletic — then there’s always going to be a chance that two passers go before them which sets the table for the Bolts picking the Heisman favorite.

In Nick Baumgardner’s latest mock, he has the Titans trading up with the Jets to pick Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker at No. 1. The Miami Dolphins then take Notre Dame’s CJ Carr at No. 2. In this scenario, that’s all it takes for the Bolts to land Smith, who currently has 86 receptions for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns through 11 games this year.

Here’s what Baumgardner had to say about the pairing with the Chargers:

“Smith would be like a swim-up bar in the desert for Justin Herbert and the Chargers, who need playmakers more than anyone right now. Jim Harbaugh’s team — specifically, his pass offense (ranked 29th in the NFL) — is floundering. Second-year receiver Tre’ Harris leads the team with 28 catches; 48 other receivers in the league have more. The Bolts are out of power there.”

“As college football’s best player, Smith should win the Heisman Trophy. Though he has the goods to become the first receiver to go No. 1 since Keyshawn Johnson in 1996, a QB or two could bump him (slightly) down the board.”

content.value:
Rookies Jake Slaughter and Logan Taylor were both forced into the starting lineup for the Chargers much earlier than either likely expected. Against the Jets, the two put on strong performances that should help ease the minds of Chargers fans who remain worried about the front five and the future depth of the group.

Taylor, a sixth-round pick out of Boston College, had his best best overall game against the Jets and finished Sunday as the team’s highest-graded offensive linemen. Slaughter, on the other hand, posted his second-best game grade of the year, trailing his current high mark by less than half a grade point.

Unfortunate it was the defense — for once — that let the whole team down on a night they failed to make the Jets punt even once. Hard to win any game when the complementary football is nowhere to be found.

Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Sunday.

Offense

Best

RB Keaton Mitchell – 89.5
OG Logan Taylor – 78.9
OT Joe Alt – 76.4
WR Ladd McConkey – 71.4
C Jake Slaughter – 68.6
RB Omarion Hampton – 68.6
QB Justin Herbert – 68.6

Mitchell played just two snaps against the Jets so his grade is a bit misleading, but he otherwise caught his lone pass of the game for a first down so at least that’s good efficiency!

Taylor ended up being the best offensive lineman against the Jets, beating out Alt by a couple grade points. He posted the team’s best run block grade at 77.6 to go with the third best pass block grade (69.2).

Alt led the way in pass protection with a 85.9 while his run block grade of 67.1 was third.

McConkey finally returned — and stayed — on the field for the entire game and wound up scoring two touchdowns whiling leading the team in both receptions and yards.

Slaughter, Hampton, and Herbert all played some of the their best football this year against New York. It was Herbert first game all year with multiple touchdown passes on top of committing no turnovers.

Worst

TE Oronde Gadsden – 46.6
OT Travis Burke – 53.0
OG Kayode Awosika – 53.2
WR Quentin Johnston – 55.8
WR Theo Wease Jr. – 56.2

Burke had very rough outing this week while facing Jets rookie pass rusher David Bailey who was this year’s third-overall pick. He allowed a sack (three pressures total) and ended with a 47.8 pass block grade.

Awosika was actually really good in pass pro against the Jets (82.0) but his run blocking left a lot to be desired as he finished with a 52.0. Somehow, that balanced out to a 53.2.

Johnston caught one pass on two targets for nine yards. His fall into irrelevancy continues.

Defense

Best
LB Troy Dye – 82.7
EDGE Bud Dupree – 79.6
CB Deane Leonard – 79.4
EDGE Caleb Murphy – 78.6
DT Justin Eboigbe – 69.6

Dye recorded the defense’s only sack while being only one of two players to record multiple pressures. His pass rush grade of 87.4 was by far the best on the team.

Leonard’s 81.0 coverage grade was tops on the team and the next best among defensive backs was nearly 20 full points lower (Tony Jefferson, 62.2).

Murphy had the defense’s second best coverage grade (76.2) and landed among the top six in both run defense (66.4) and tackling (73.9).

Eboigbe’s 71.4 run defense grade second on the team only to safety Elijah Molden.

Worst

CB Donte Jackson – 28.1
DT Teair Tart – 29.1
DT Dalvin Tomlinson – 38.5
S Genesis Smith – 42.2
S R.J. Mickens – 46.3

Jackson would probably like to forget Sunday’s performance as soon as possible. He finished with five catches allowed for 71 yards and three touchdowns. He also missed a pair of tackles. Not great!

Tart posted a 29.0 run defense grade, marking his worst performance of the season in that area. His pass rush grade of 52.2 was also tied for worst on the team.

Smith posted the second worst tackling (27.6) and coverage grades (40.1) for the Chargers. He missed two tackles, well.

Mickens finsihed with poor marks across the board with lowlights coming in coverage (49.6) and tackling (42.5).

content.value:
The Chargers started on a lower note than the Jets on Sunday and they never quite were able to flip the script, even if the game eventually came down to the final minutes.

Justin Herbert, for the first time this year, threw multiple touchdown passes in the same game while the entire offense avoided turning the ball over altogether. Unfortunately, for the first time against a lowly opponent, Chris O’Leary’s defense faltered. They were down starting players Daiyan Henley and Tarheeb Still, and it seemed to show as Geno Smith and Co. put up 341 yards and 27 points.

Even with the loss dropping the team to 1-9 on the year, CBS Sports’ John Breech still gave the Chargers a respectable “B” grade for their performance. Here’s what he had to say:

“The Chargers defense might have finally hit rock bottom. They didn’t force the Jets to punt a single time and if you don’t get any stops, that forces your offense to play perfect football and the Chargers just don’t have the offensive talent to play perfect football this year. The offense was good against the Jets, but it could have been better if the offensive line could have protected Justin Herbert. The Chargers QB got sacked six times, but the offense was still able to move the ball thanks to a suddenly revived rushing attack that went off for 158 yards, the team’s second-highest total of the season. The Chargers’ lost season has somehow gone from bad to worse.”

content.value:
Week 11 ended in a less-than-ideal way for the Los Angeles Chargers in more ways than one.

Not only did the Chargers drop their Week 11 matchup to the New York Jets with a final score of 27-24; the team announced postgame that quarterback Justin Herbert will enter the concussion protocol.

Herbert was able to play for the entire game, going 15 of 21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns, no picks, and he took six sacks, which begins to explain the concussion. The Chargers were in this one right up until the end, but the Jets did just enough to snap their five-game losing streak and keep the Chargers from establishing a win streak for the first time this season.

The Chargers are technically not eliminated from postseason contention, but they are tied with the Dolphins and Titans for the worst record in the NFL at 1-9. And losing Herbert is unlikely to help.

DJ Uiagalelei is the next man up on the Chargers’ QB depth chart. The second-year signal caller signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after spending time at Clemson, Oregon State, and Florida State in college. He spent the 2025 season on the Chargers’ practice squad, and signed a futures contract with the team last offseason. He competed for the Chargers’ backup position behind Herbert with Trey Lance, but won the job when Lance landed on injured reserve in October. In 2026, he’s attempted seven passes, completing two, for 24 yards and a touchdown.

Trey Lance is currently on IR with a groin injury, but he is eligible to return at any point. There is no other quarterback on the Chargers’ active roster.

content.value:
The Chargers unfortunately fell short against the Jets 27-24 on Sunday and dropped to 1-9 on the year with seven games remaining. A miraculous late game run to push for a winning record is now impossible and all of you who held out hope for such a thing can now finally let that one go.

Another loss further reinforced the Chargers as one of the league’s worst. With a chance to get out of the bottom three in the league, the defense unfortunately could not find any decent footing as the Jets went the entire game without a single punt.

Offensively it was a better day for Justin Herbert and that unit, but overall it wasn’t enough to beat a previously 2-win Jets team.

With that said, let’s get into the rankings from Week 12.

NFL.com – #29

“After finally winning a game in Week 10, the Chargers returned to their former selves, minus the crushing turnovers. A remarkably quick game saw just 12 possessions combined between the two teams, and the Chargers didn’t quite value them as much as they should have in Sunday’s loss. A complete lack of urgency while facing a 10-point deficit frustrated everyone taking the time to watch this game and included a sequence of snaps that featured a flea flicker on third-and-2, a speed option run by a quarterback (Justin Herbert) who had already taken too many hits, and a pace that ate up nearly eight minutes of time in the fourth quarter. This is an unserious team that unsurprisingly didn’t regain possession after that marathon scoring drive and might not win another game if it continues operating like this.”

Pro Football Talk – #30

“Will Jim Harbaugh be back for 2027?” – Mike Florio

ESPN – #31

“The best player on the Chargers this season is playing out his rookie deal, so the best candidate for an extension is fairly obvious. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Tuipulotu leads the team with 37 pressures through Sunday. Are the Chargers willing to pay him top edge money, which could be close to $35 million per year? Only time will tell.” – Aaron Schatz

The Athletic – #31

“The sooner this season ends, the better. And this game lasted only 2 hours, 40 minutes, the shortest of the year. The Chargers and Jets had only six possessions apiece Sunday. New York scored on its first five, marking a rare occasion when the defense let down Los Angeles. The Chargers are now next to last in the league in offensive EPA per drive (minus-0.80).” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff

CBS Sports – #31

“After winning at Baltimore, they were back to being the Chargers again, losing to the Jets. This team has to make changes.”

Sports Illustrated – #31

“On the MMQB pod, Albert Breer breathlessly details the potential death knell in the Jim Harbaugh era: a long, meandering drive to nowhere with the game on the line.” – Conor Orr

Yahoo Sports – #32

“Good thing the Chargers got that win in Week 10. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again.“

“At least there were a couple of decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It’s not much, especially in a loss. But it’s not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.”

Sporting News – #32

“The Chargers played a clean game for the most part, but still lost to the Jets because of a key stat: Giving up six sacks on Justin Herbert. He’s been dropped 39 times in 10 games, the most in the league. The offensive line injuries continue to have lingering effects.” – Vinnie Iyer

The Chargers went and won their first game against the Ravens in Week 11 but followed that with yet another loss this past Sunday against the Jets. They’re now 1-9 with seven games to go.

If the Chargers continue their losing ways, they will stay in the mix for one of the top players in the upcoming draft class. Obviously Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith is the crown jewel of the group, but will the Bolts truly have a shot at taking Smith if they don’t pick number one overall?

To be quite honest, yes, they could.

Quarterbacks always end up being the biggest priority amongst the league’s worst teams. If the Chargers end up picking at No. 3 — like they do in this new mock at The Athletic — then there’s always going to be a chance that two passers go before them which sets the table for the Bolts picking the Heisman favorite.

In Nick Baumgardner’s latest mock, he has the Titans trading up with the Jets to pick Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker at No. 1. The Miami Dolphins then take Notre Dame’s CJ Carr at No. 2. In this scenario, that’s all it takes for the Bolts to land Smith, who currently has 86 receptions for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns through 11 games this year.

Here’s what Baumgardner had to say about the pairing with the Chargers:

“Smith would be like a swim-up bar in the desert for Justin Herbert and the Chargers, who need playmakers more than anyone right now. Jim Harbaugh’s team — specifically, his pass offense (ranked 29th in the NFL) — is floundering. Second-year receiver Tre’ Harris leads the team with 28 catches; 48 other receivers in the league have more. The Bolts are out of power there.”

“As college football’s best player, Smith should win the Heisman Trophy. Though he has the goods to become the first receiver to go No. 1 since Keyshawn Johnson in 1996, a QB or two could bump him (slightly) down the board.”

content.value:
Rookies Jake Slaughter and Logan Taylor were both forced into the starting lineup for the Chargers much earlier than either likely expected. Against the Jets, the two put on strong performances that should help ease the minds of Chargers fans who remain worried about the front five and the future depth of the group.

Taylor, a sixth-round pick out of Boston College, had his best best overall game against the Jets and finished Sunday as the team’s highest-graded offensive linemen. Slaughter, on the other hand, posted his second-best game grade of the year, trailing his current high mark by less than half a grade point.

Unfortunate it was the defense — for once — that let the whole team down on a night they failed to make the Jets punt even once. Hard to win any game when the complementary football is nowhere to be found.

Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Sunday.

Offense

Best

RB Keaton Mitchell – 89.5
OG Logan Taylor – 78.9
OT Joe Alt – 76.4
WR Ladd McConkey – 71.4
C Jake Slaughter – 68.6
RB Omarion Hampton – 68.6
QB Justin Herbert – 68.6

Mitchell played just two snaps against the Jets so his grade is a bit misleading, but he otherwise caught his lone pass of the game for a first down so at least that’s good efficiency!

Taylor ended up being the best offensive lineman against the Jets, beating out Alt by a couple grade points. He posted the team’s best run block grade at 77.6 to go with the third best pass block grade (69.2).

Alt led the way in pass protection with a 85.9 while his run block grade of 67.1 was third.

McConkey finally returned — and stayed — on the field for the entire game and wound up scoring two touchdowns whiling leading the team in both receptions and yards.

Slaughter, Hampton, and Herbert all played some of the their best football this year against New York. It was Herbert first game all year with multiple touchdown passes on top of committing no turnovers.

Worst

TE Oronde Gadsden – 46.6
OT Travis Burke – 53.0
OG Kayode Awosika – 53.2
WR Quentin Johnston – 55.8
WR Theo Wease Jr. – 56.2

Burke had very rough outing this week while facing Jets rookie pass rusher David Bailey who was this year’s third-overall pick. He allowed a sack (three pressures total) and ended with a 47.8 pass block grade.

Awosika was actually really good in pass pro against the Jets (82.0) but his run blocking left a lot to be desired as he finished with a 52.0. Somehow, that balanced out to a 53.2.

Johnston caught one pass on two targets for nine yards. His fall into irrelevancy continues.

Defense

Best
LB Troy Dye – 82.7
EDGE Bud Dupree – 79.6
CB Deane Leonard – 79.4
EDGE Caleb Murphy – 78.6
DT Justin Eboigbe – 69.6

Dye recorded the defense’s only sack while being only one of two players to record multiple pressures. His pass rush grade of 87.4 was by far the best on the team.

Leonard’s 81.0 coverage grade was tops on the team and the next best among defensive backs was nearly 20 full points lower (Tony Jefferson, 62.2).

Murphy had the defense’s second best coverage grade (76.2) and landed among the top six in both run defense (66.4) and tackling (73.9).

Eboigbe’s 71.4 run defense grade second on the team only to safety Elijah Molden.

Worst

CB Donte Jackson – 28.1
DT Teair Tart – 29.1
DT Dalvin Tomlinson – 38.5
S Genesis Smith – 42.2
S R.J. Mickens – 46.3

Jackson would probably like to forget Sunday’s performance as soon as possible. He finished with five catches allowed for 71 yards and three touchdowns. He also missed a pair of tackles. Not great!

Tart posted a 29.0 run defense grade, marking his worst performance of the season in that area. His pass rush grade of 52.2 was also tied for worst on the team.

Smith posted the second worst tackling (27.6) and coverage grades (40.1) for the Chargers. He missed two tackles, well.

Mickens finsihed with poor marks across the board with lowlights coming in coverage (49.6) and tackling (42.5).

The Chargers started on a lower note than the Jets on Sunday and they never quite were able to flip the script, even if the game eventually came down to the final minutes.

Justin Herbert, for the first time this year, threw multiple touchdown passes in the same game while the entire offense avoided turning the ball over altogether. Unfortunately, for the first time against a lowly opponent, Chris O’Leary’s defense faltered. They were down starting players Daiyan Henley and Tarheeb Still, and it seemed to show as Geno Smith and Co. put up 341 yards and 27 points.

Even with the loss dropping the team to 1-9 on the year, CBS Sports’ John Breech still gave the Chargers a respectable “B” grade for their performance. Here’s what he had to say:

“The Chargers defense might have finally hit rock bottom. They didn’t force the Jets to punt a single time and if you don’t get any stops, that forces your offense to play perfect football and the Chargers just don’t have the offensive talent to play perfect football this year. The offense was good against the Jets, but it could have been better if the offensive line could have protected Justin Herbert. The Chargers QB got sacked six times, but the offense was still able to move the ball thanks to a suddenly revived rushing attack that went off for 158 yards, the team’s second-highest total of the season. The Chargers’ lost season has somehow gone from bad to worse.”

content.value:
Week 11 ended in a less-than-ideal way for the Los Angeles Chargers in more ways than one.

Not only did the Chargers drop their Week 11 matchup to the New York Jets with a final score of 27-24; the team announced postgame that quarterback Justin Herbert will enter the concussion protocol.

Herbert was able to play for the entire game, going 15 of 21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns, no picks, and he took six sacks, which begins to explain the concussion. The Chargers were in this one right up until the end, but the Jets did just enough to snap their five-game losing streak and keep the Chargers from establishing a win streak for the first time this season.

The Chargers are technically not eliminated from postseason contention, but they are tied with the Dolphins and Titans for the worst record in the NFL at 1-9. And losing Herbert is unlikely to help.

DJ Uiagalelei is the next man up on the Chargers’ QB depth chart. The second-year signal caller signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent in 2025 after spending time at Clemson, Oregon State, and Florida State in college. He spent the 2025 season on the Chargers’ practice squad, and signed a futures contract with the team last offseason. He competed for the Chargers’ backup position behind Herbert with Trey Lance, but won the job when Lance landed on injured reserve in October. In 2026, he’s attempted seven passes, completing two, for 24 yards and a touchdown.

Trey Lance is currently on IR with a groin injury, but he is eligible to return at any point. There is no other quarterback on the Chargers’ active roster.

We will monitor this situation and update as more information becomes available.

content.value:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-9 after falling to the New York Jets at home in Week 11. Now the Chargers will have a chance to go up against the New England Patriots at home in Week 12.

The Patriots are coming off their bye week, which was much needed after their Week 10 loss against the Detroit Lions in Munich, where they lost Drake Maye to an ankle injury that could keep him out for the rest of the year. This means Tommy DeVito is set to start for the Pats against the Chargers, which gives Los Angeles a chance to pull out its second win of the season.

The Bolts entered this week as 1.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The over/under is currently set at 37.5 points.

The Chargers killed some of their momentum after beating the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, with a loss against the New York Jets. The Chargers trailed 17-3 with 3 minutes to go in the second quarter, forcing them to mount a comeback.

While Justin Herbert ran for a touchdown as time expired in the first half and completed two touchdowns to Ladd McConkey in the fourth quarter, they ultimately fell short by a field goal against the Jets.

Herbert entered the league’s concussion protocol following the game, and his status is up in the air for the contest against the Patriots.

content.value:
The Los Angeles Chargers are getting ready for their Week 11 matchup against the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium.

While most of the players are getting ready, a few members of the team will be on the inactive list.

LB Daiyan Henley, CB Tarheeb Still, S Kendall Williamson, G Alex Harkey, WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith and WR Brenen Thompson are all out for the Chargers against the Jets.

  • Henley was already ruled out on the injury report, as he has been out of practice all week with a knee injury.
  • Thompson was doubtful, as he’s been dealing with a lingering hamstring injury.
  • Williamson was limited in practice at the beginning of the week but did not practice on Thursday or Friday, ruling him out for the contest.
  • Still was still questionable with an ankle injury, but he has also been ruled out.
  • Harkey and Lambert-Smith are healthy scratches.

Meanwhile, the inactives for the Jets are CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr., WR Omar Cooper Jr., WR Isaiah Williams, LB Trevin Wallace, TE Jelani Woods and EDGE Nate Lynn.

Kickoff between the Jets and Chargers is set for 1:05 p.m. PT inside SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

content.value:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-8 going into their Week 11 matchup against the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium.

The Chargers can breathe a sigh of relief as they won’t go winless, but they have lost the inside path to the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

In this week’s Reacts poll, 43% of fans said they would be okay if the Chargers didn’t get the No. 1 overall pick.

The Chargers would have the chance to trade out of the pick with a team looking to select a quarterback, or they could take someone like Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which could completely change their offense.

In last week’s Reacts poll, the confidence meter to determine whether the team is heading in the right direction, is at 13 percent.

It’s a slight step down from the 14 percent mark the team was at last week, but one win isn’t enough to rebuild all of the confidence zapped from the eight-game losing streak to start the season.

The Chargers are hoping to win their first home game of the year against the Jets at SoFi Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 pm PT. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.
